newsitem.title: USA: Wabash sees earnings pressure relief.
newsitem.headline: Wabash sees earnings pressure relief.

text.p: Wabash National Corp said Monday it expects the factors which pushed its third quarter earnings lower to improve.

Wabash said $20 million in higher-margin European trailers were produced but revenues were deferred into the fourth quarter, and the production of plate trailers was restricted because of a limited supply of materials, which is easing.
As a result, commodity trailers were a higher percentage of sales, and pricing of these trailers has been under extreme pressure, Wabash said.
Wabash reported third quarter earnings of $0.01 a share versus $0.31 a share last year.

Jerry Ehrlich, chairman, president and chief executive of Wabash, said the factors "are anticipated to improve with the international revenues being recognized, continued ramp-up of the composite plate trailer production and the possibility for improved market conditions as a result of industry consolidation."
The company said it continues to invest in new markets.
"The development of these new products and new markets impact margins short term, but represent opportunities for growth in higher margin segments," Ehrlich said in a statement.
